_about: fak position rows for the 'operability' group. dim_id links each to a _taxonomy.json dimension.

rows.axis: Fairness, priority, and tenant isolation in batch formation / scheduling
rows.competitor: FairBatching (fairness-aware batch formation); SGLang (FCFS + page-eviction preemption); hybrid real-time/best-effort schedulers (e.g. arXiv 2504.09590)
rows.fak_doc: No fairness / priority-class / tenant-isolation batch-formation number in BENCHMARK-AUTHORITY.md or CLAIMS.md. fak ships per-agent KV ownership and causal cache invalidation (BENCHMARK-AUTHORITY.md causal-invalidation witness, max|delta|=0) but no measured head-of-line-blocking or priority-preemption behavior.
rows.comparison_note: OUT OF SCOPE as a measured serving-fairness number, though adjacent to fak's trust plane: fak provides per-agent KV isolation and targeted causal eviction (witnessed bit-exact), but it has no FairBatching-style per-request unfairness bound, no priority classes with preemption, and no measured head-of-line-blocking behavior in batch formation. The SOTA bar here is itself qualitative; fak still has no number, so no claim.

rows.axis: Latency degradation under concurrency / load (saturation behavior)
rows.competitor: vLLM benchmark_serving (request-rate sweep); NVIDIA GenAI-Perf (concurrency sweep)
rows.unit: RPS at which P99 TTFT crosses SLO
rows.fak_doc: The GPU server concurrency sweep (conc 1->128, QWEN36-27B-GPU-SERVER-RESULTS.md) varies LOAD but records completion-tokens/sec, not a TTFT/queueing curve: there is no committed P99-TTFT-vs-RPS saturation sweep showing the rate at which the SLO is crossed.
rows.comparison_note: REAL GAP fak should measure. fak has the harness to vary concurrency (it ran 1->128 on the GPU server) but reports the throughput envelope, not the saturation diagnostic (P99 TTFT climbing while P50 stays flat as the queue builds). Since the gateway proxy adds queueing of its own, the TTFT-under-load curve is exactly what an honest operability claim needs; not yet measured, so no-claim.

rows.fak_doc: internal/gateway/startup.go emits fak_gateway_time_to_ready_seconds plus per-phase startup duration; internal/gateway/readiness_warmup.go can hold readiness until a representative warmup turn completes; docs/notes/GLM52-COLD-START-VS-CACHING-ABLATION-2026-07-06.md records the observed ~500 s backend warmup separately from KV reuse. No comparable scale-to-zero / scale-out latency result is committed.
rows.comparison_note: PARTIAL SURFACE SHIPPED; no comparable scale-to-zero claim. fak now measures boot-to-ready and named startup phases, and its optional warmup gate keeps /healthz unready until a representative first token so the operator's first real request does not absorb a known cold backend warmup. The committed GLM-5.2 observation (~500 s cold warmup versus ~1 s warm turns) is a real cold-start diagnostic, but it is not an apples-to-apples serverless snapshot / scale-out benchmark and fak still ships no autoscaler or scale-to-zero lifecycle. The full axis therefore remains no-claim rather than converting the non-comparable observation into a manufactured trail.

rows.axis: Cross-instance / persistent KV cache sharing and coherence
rows.fak_doc: CLAIMS lines 66-71: recall persists a finished session as a durable, integrity-checked CORE IMAGE reloadable in a FRESH process; BENCHMARK-AUTHORITY causal-invalidation row proves a coherence-bus broadcast + targeted causal eviction (max|Δ|=0). But this is cross-PROCESS session reload + invalidation coherence, not a live cross-INSTANCE shared KV POOL like LMCache/Mooncake Store.
rows.comparison_note: REAL GAP, with adjacent mechanism shipped. fak has durable cross-process session core images and a coherence bus that broadcasts cache refutations with byte-exact causal eviction, but NOT a global deduplicated KV pool shared across live engine instances (LMCache cross-instance reuse / Mooncake Store). The pieces that point toward it (recall, the coherence bus, the not-yet-witness-keyed tier-2) are real; the cross-instance live-sharing claim is unbuilt, so no parity is asserted.

rows.axis: Multi-node fault tolerance & failure recovery (resilient serving)
rows.unit: mean-time-to-recovery / sustained throughput under GPU loss
rows.fak_doc: none — no multi-node failure-recovery number in CLAIMS; causal-invalidation (commit 0fc39aa) is an integrity/coherence witness, not failure recovery
rows.comparison_note: OUT OF SCOPE for a single-box reuse kernel. fak has no multi-node serving topology, hence no node-failure rerouting, no background KV replication, no decoupled parallel re-init. Its nearest adjacent witness — causal invalidation-on-external-write (vdso.Revoke, commit 0fc39aa, max|Delta|=0) — is an INTEGRITY/coherence property (evict cache reads a write made stale), explicitly 'a containment/coherence witness, not a throughput number', NOT failure recovery. The research bar (KevlarFlow/FailSafe/ReviveMoE) is multi-GPU resilient serving fak does not attempt. No fak number; verdict no-claim.

rows.axis: OpenAI-compatible API surface + reliable structured output / tool-calling
rows.unit: OpenAI-compat surface present (capability), structured-output rung depth
rows.fak_doc: CLAIMS.md Gateway [SHIPPED] (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses, /v1/models, /healthz, MCP); Engine [SHIPPED] OpenAI-compatible client base_url-swappable; internal/agent forwards response_format / logit_bias carriers; internal/model constraint_test.go witnesses the opt-in FAK_NATIVE_GUIDED_DECODE per-step LogitMask before argmax
rows.comparison_note: Parity on CAPABILITY PRESENCE, not a JSON-schema conformance or guided-decoding performance number. fak ships the de facto OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions and Responses surfaces, forwards structured-output carriers to ridden OpenAI-compatible engines, and now owns an opt-in in-kernel decode-time constraint hook: logit_bias and an injected per-step LogitMask apply before argmax, with a deterministic load-bearing schema-valid JSON witness. The remaining gap versus XGrammar-2 is breadth and measurement: no committed arbitrary-schema conformance percentage, grammar-compile coverage, or per-token overhead comparison. apples_to_apples=false keeps this a bounded API + mechanism parity claim, not an unqualified guided-decoding parity claim.

rows.axis: Production observability: Prometheus metrics (TTFT/TPOT/queue) + OpenTelemetry tracing
rows.unit: metric-set coverage vs the vLLM TTFT/TPOT/queue/cache-hit + OTel contract
rows.fak_doc: CLAIMS.md [SHIPPED] Serving-latency observability; internal/gateway/metrics_render.go emits fak_gateway_inference_ttft_seconds, fak_gateway_inference_tpot_seconds, fak_gateway_inference_e2e_seconds, inflight / KV-memory / prefix-reuse families, and provider cache-hit ratio; internal/gateway/serving_metrics.go emits the normalized fak_serving_* serving families. W3C trace-context propagation and OTLP span export are not shipped (#5629).
rows.comparison_note: METRIC-SET PARITY; DISTRIBUTED-TRACING GAP. The native surface emits fak_gateway_inference_ttft_seconds, fak_gateway_inference_tpot_seconds, and fak_gateway_inference_e2e_seconds; fak_gateway_inflight_requests, fak_gateway_inflight_requests_by_route, and fak_gateway_inflight_max_age_seconds; fak_gateway_kv_memory_resident_bytes, fak_gateway_kv_memory_capacity_bytes, and fak_gateway_kv_memory_headroom_ratio; fak_gateway_kv_prefix_reuse_ratio; and fak_gateway_inference_cached_prompt_hit_ratio. The normalized serving schema emits fak_serving_time_to_first_token_seconds, fak_serving_time_per_output_token_seconds, fak_serving_inter_token_latency_seconds, fak_serving_num_requests_running, fak_serving_num_requests_waiting, fak_serving_kv_cache_usage_perc, and fak_serving_prefix_cache_hit_rate for native or ridden workers. The separate [SIMULATED] metrics-service scrape adapter is not needed as evidence for this native surface and is intentionally omitted from the grounds. What is still absent is W3C trace-context propagation (traceparent/tracestate) and OTLP/OpenTelemetry span export: X-Trace-Id supplies fak-local correlation, not standards-based distributed tracing (#5629). Because this axis combines the serving metric set with OpenTelemetry, the composite honestly trails even though the named Prometheus metric set is at parity.

rows.competitor: KServe + KEDA; Ray Serve; llm-d / vLLM on Kubernetes
rows.fak_doc: deploy/k8s/fak.yaml + kustomization.yaml ship an apply-ready hardened proxy Deployment/Service/Secret/ConfigMap; deploy/k8s/overlays/gpu ships the in-kernel one-GPU/PVC sibling; docs/fak/deployment-guide.md is the operator contract. No fak-owned KEDA/HPA/operator or scale-to-zero controller is shipped.
rows.comparison_note: KUBERNETES DEPLOYMENT SHIPPED; LLM-AWARE AUTOSCALING UNBUILT. fak now has copy-paste base and GPU-overlay manifests with liveness/readiness probes, hardened pod settings, kustomize entry points, and a documented rollout/smoke path. That removes the old 'no K8s deployment' claim. The scored contract is broader, however: fak still has no KServe/KEDA/Ray operator, no custom-metric HPA driven by running/waiting requests, no traffic-split/canary controller, and no scale-to-zero lifecycle. apples_to_apples=false and no-claim preserve that residual rather than treating deployability alone as autoscaling parity.

rows.axis: Multi-tenant fairness, per-tenant quotas, and SLO attainment under contention
rows.competitor: VTC (Sheng et al.); LiteLLM (virtual keys/budgets); Equinox / FairBatching
rows.unit: per-tenant fairness / SLO attainment under contention
rows.fak_doc: internal/gateway/token_admission_principal.go gives each authenticated principal an isolated rolling-window token allotment; internal/gateway/spend_governor.go + fak serve --spend-cap enforce tenant/team/agent/session token or USD caps across the served boundary. No VTC-style fair scheduler or per-tenant SLO-under-contention benchmark is committed.
rows.comparison_note: TENANT QUOTA/BUDGET HALF SHIPPED; FAIR-SCHEDULING/SLO HALF UNBUILT. Authenticated org/project principals now receive isolated token-rate allotments, so one noisy tenant cannot consume another's allotment, and control-plane spend caps can bound the aggregate token/USD spend of every session under a tenant. That removes the old 'no per-tenant quotas or spend caps' claim. fak still has no work-conserving VTC/FairBatching-style scheduler, no priority-preemption policy keyed by tenant, and no measured per-tenant SLO attainment under contention. The full fairness axis therefore remains no-claim, with apples_to_apples=false to separate shipped governance quotas from serving-scheduler fairness.
